subject: Re: MSA - Indemnity trigger mapping & ops handoff
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fastlane.health>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: procurements@fastlane.health
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA - Indemnity trigger & ops handoff

Hi Jasmine / Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare to move to contract, Procurement asked us to confirm two things before signature: (1) precise triggers for Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims arising from model output, and (2) the operational handoff if a claim is reported (who on Redwood owns triage, evidence requests, and legal coordination).

We're concerned about timing (notice windows) and evidence flow — we need a short trusted path so our security and legal teams can meet their SLA to our board. Can you share a proposed mapping (trigger => owner => SLA) and any existing runbook you would expect to use?

Attached: claim_flow_template.xlsx (shows our preferred evidence checklist).

Elena Rossi
Head of Legal Operations
Fastlane Health
elena.rossi@fastlane.health

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fastlane.health>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA - Indemnity trigger & ops handoff

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the template.

Quick responses: we can map triggers into three buckets (1) provable third-party infringement where customer content is primary cause, (2) model training IP claims (edge cases), and (3) downstream output-only claims (harder case). For each bucket we'll propose an owner (Redwood legal / Redwood infra / customer) and a 72/120 hour initial response SLA depending on severity.

Next steps from our side: Kimberly will propose redline language that clarifies notice and cooperation obligations without expanding scope beyond industry norms. From ops, Aditya will draft a lean runbook that defines contact points, evidence staging (where we store logs/kv cache snapshots), and escalation criteria.

I've attached a lightweight copy of Fastlane's template to annotate; can you confirm the three-week signature target on your side? If procurement needs us to shorten notice windows we'll flag that in the redline.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Counsel, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fastlane.health>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA - Indemnity trigger & ops handoff

Elena / Jasmine —

I reviewed Fastlane's template and sketched a targeted redline focused on three items that typically cause pushback: notice triggers, cap/warranty interplay, and control of defense (choice of counsel). Key proposals in the draft:

- Narrow the trigger to claims "arising from Customer Content or Customer-provided prompts" and exclude general output that cannot be tied to a customer prompt unless Fastlane supplies the prompt or dataset.
- Maintain carveouts for open-source model pre-existing IP where appropriate (we propose a mutual OSS schedule).
- For defense control, we proposed a hybrid approach: Redwood will have right to assume defense for third-party IP claims but must offer co-counsel and accept customer's insurance-limited vendors for jurisdictional needs.

I attached MSA_redline_indemnity.docx with inline comments and a short redline summary at the top. I highlighted the notice timing options (30/60/90 days) — recommend 60 days as a reasonable compromise given evidence staging needs.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Regulatory, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Elena / team —

From an ops/sales perspective, a short mutual action plan (MAP) that ties contract language to a single on-call incident queue will reduce friction post-signature. Proposal highlights:

- Primary contact: Redwood Trust & Safety (ts-claims@redwood.com) for triage; Legal looped in within 4 hours of triage decision.
- Evidence staging: we can accept a pre-authorized temporary S3 bucket with read-only access for your legal team for 30 days; logs and model kv snapshots stored for 90 days by default.
- Escalation ladder: Triage -> Incident Lead (ops) -> Legal -> Executive sponsor.

I started an ops outline: ops_runbook_outline.md (link in Drive). If this aligns, we can bake the MAP into an appendix to the order form so it becomes operationally actionable on day one.

Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — this is really helpful.

Procurement confirms the three-week signature target is still on the table provided we can land on notice timing and a defensible MAP. Fastlane is comfortable with a 60-day notice window and the hybrid defense-control approach you proposed, subject to (1) a short escalation SLA (48 hours) for initial triage acceptance, and (2) a clause that Redwood will preserve KV cache snapshots and request logs for at least 60 days if a claim is reported.

We reviewed the Drive outline and the redline. Next steps from Fastlane: we'll run your redline by in-house counsel this week and return a marked copy by EOD Friday. Can Redwood confirm a single point of contact for evidence transfer and a DocuSign-ready version of the MAP appendix?

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal Operations
Fastlane Health
